questions.title: Four friends, shoe brands and sizes
questions.statement:
Four friends, David, Max, John, and Shane, went shopping. Each purchased shoes from four different brands – Pima, Avidas, Fola, and Nikiy – in different sizes: 7, 8, 9, and 10, but not necessarily in the same order.

- David purchased from either Pima or Fola and his shoe size is a perfect square.
- Shane purchased a shoe of a prime number size from Nikiy.
- The person who purchased a perfect cube-size shoe is of the brand Fola.
- John didn't purchase from Fola.

Which of the given options is the correct combination of Person-Shoe size-Brand?
options: David-7-Pima
Max-9-Fola
John-10-Avidas
Shane-7-Avidas
questions.explanation: David's size is the only perfect square, 9. Shane's size is the only prime, 7, and his brand is Nikiy. Size 8 (the cube) is Fola, so David (size 9) must be Pima. John is not Fola, so John is 10 and Max is 8-Fola. The remaining brand, Avidas, goes to John: John-10-Avidas.

questions.title: Six girls in a row - who is at the left end
questions.statement:
Six girls, namely Olivia, Quinn, Rachel, Nia, Sara, and Tara, are sitting in a row, facing North, but not necessarily in the same order.

- There are three girls sitting between Rachel and Sara.
- Tara is to the immediate right of Sara but is not at either end of the row.
- Olivia is neither adjacent to Tara nor Rachel.

Who is sitting at the left end of the row?
options: Rachel
Olivia
Tara
Nia
questions.explanation: Number the seats 1-6 from the left. Rachel and Sara are 4 apart, and Tara sits at Sara+1 but not at an end. That leaves two cases: (S1, T2, R5) or (S2, T3, R6). In case 1, every free seat (3, 4, 6) is next to Tara or Rachel, so Olivia has nowhere to sit. In case 2, Olivia can only take seat 1, so Olivia is at the left end.

questions.pattern: reverse word then alternate +1/-1 letter shift
questions.title: Coding-decoding: ROCKET, WISELY, MARKET
questions.statement: If 'ROCKET' is coded as 'UDLBPQ' and 'WISELY' is coded as 'ZKFRJV', then how will 'MARKET' be coded in the same language?
options: USBFLN
UDLQBL
LNFBSU
UTBFSL
questions.explanation: Reverse the word, then shift the letters alternately by +1 and -1. ROCKET reversed is TEKCOR, which gives U D L B P Q. MARKET reversed is TEKRAM, which gives T+1=U, E-1=D, K+1=L, R-1=Q, A+1=B, M-1=L, i.e. UDLQBL.

questions.pattern: height comparison - deduce truth of fourth statement
questions.title: Six people heights - is Q or R the shortest
questions.statement:
Six people, P, Q, R, S, T, and U, each having a different height, are comparing their heights.

I. P is taller than Q but not the tallest.
II. R is shorter than S.
III. T is shorter than U but taller than at least three people.
IV. Either Q or R is the shortest.

If the first three statements are true, what can be said about the fourth statement?
options: True
False
Uncertain
questions.explanation: P (taller than Q), S (taller than R), U (taller than T) and T (taller than at least three people) each have someone shorter than them, so none of them can be the shortest. Only Q or R can be the shortest, so statement IV is True.

questions.pattern: rank from top and bottom - total count
questions.title: Class ranking - total number of students
questions.statement: Each student in a class test ranking list is assigned a unique rank based on their performance. Alex is ranked $10^{th}$ from the top, while Ben is ranked $18^{th}$ from the bottom of the list. If Alex's rank is eight positions higher than Ben's rank in the list, then how many students are there in the class?
options: None of the mentioned options
questions.explanation: Ben is 8 places below Alex, so Ben is 18th from the top. He is also 18th from the bottom, so the total is 18 + 18 - 1 = 35.

questions.pattern: zig-zag direction sense with increasing steps
questions.title: Girl walking north-south with increasing distances
questions.statement:
A girl walked 10 m North and then turned and moved 20 m South. She repeated this pattern, increasing her distance by 10 m each time she turned and moved in the opposite direction. After her last turn, she covered a distance of 60 m. Following that, she walked 30 m straight to her right.

What is the shortest distance between the girl's final point and her starting point?
questions.explanation: The legs are 10N, 20S, 30N, 40S, 50N, 60S. North total = 90 and south total = 120, so she ends 30 m south while facing south. Her right is then west, so she walks 30 m west. The distance is $\sqrt{30^2+30^2}=30\sqrt{2}$ m.

questions.pattern: sentence word-code matching by common words
questions.title: Word coding: play can win
questions.statement: If "you can win" is coded as "joe nee sop", "can you do" is coded as "sop nee tee" and "do you play" is coded as "nee sow tee", then how is "play can win" coded in that language?
options: sop sow joe
sop tee joe
nee tee sow
joe tee sow
questions.explanation: 'you' appears in all three phrases, so you = nee. The words shared by phrases 1 and 2 give can = sop, which leaves win = joe. Phrases 2 and 3 give do = tee, which leaves play = sow. So 'play can win' is coded with sow, sop and joe: option 'sop sow joe'.

questions.pattern: age comparison - deduce truth of fourth statement
questions.title: Five people ages - greatest age difference
questions.statement:
There are five people, P, Q, R, S, and T, such that:

I. P is older than Q.
II. R is not older than P.
III. S is older than T, but Q is older than S.
IV. The greatest age difference is between P and T.

If the first three statements are true, what can be said about the fourth statement?
options: True
False
Uncertain
questions.explanation: The order is P > Q > S > T, with R younger than P. P is the oldest, but R could be younger than T, so the youngest is either T or R. Statement IV is therefore Uncertain.

questions.title: Management lesson - self-control and success
questions.statement:
In the field of management, the most important lesson that we need to learn is that one should ensure success in an endeavor. The subjects taught in management are mere tools for achieving what management is trying to teach subtly. Human psychologists believe that success can be ensured through behavioral elements such as determination. Enhancing determination using self-control is the first step towards achieving success in every sphere of life.

If the above statement is true, then which of the following can be inferred?
options: Self-control is a factor that can lead to success in life.
There is only one step towards achieving success in life.
Anyone who is successful would surely have greater self-control.
Achieving success in life can happen only with determination.
questions.answer: Self-control is a factor that can lead to success in life.
questions.explanation: The passage says self-control is the first step towards success, so it is a contributing factor. 'Only one step', 'surely' and 'only with' are all claims stronger than the passage supports.

questions.notes: Section titled 'Critical Thinking' in the OA.

questions.title: Declining US saving rate - weaken the education program
questions.statement:
An economic advisory report published in 2006 said: The personal saving rate in the United States has declined steadily from 10 percent of after-tax income in 1972 to 2 percent of after-tax income in 2005. Financial experts suggest that every person must save at least 10 percent of after-tax income to be able to meet retirement, healthcare or unexpected expenses. Therefore, the government must launch a program to educate citizens about the importance of saving at least 10 percent of their after-tax income.

Which of the given statements, if true, most seriously calls into question the recommendation above?
options: From 1972 to 2005, the percentage of United States citizens with zero or negative non-home wealth increased from 24 percent to 28 percent.
From 1972 to 2005, the average cost of living of a United States citizen increased by 80 percent while the average annual after-tax income increased only by 10 percent.
From 1972 to 2005, the average credit-card debt per an indebted United States citizen increased sixteen times.
From 1972 to 2005, the per capita private healthcare expenditure increased by 600 percent.
questions.answer: From 1972 to 2005, the average cost of living of a United States citizen increased by 80 percent while the average annual after-tax income increased only by 10 percent.
questions.explanation: If costs grew much faster than income, people save less because they cannot afford to, not because they are unaware. An education program would then not fix the problem.
source_files: Company wise prep resource-20261001T122326Z-1-001\Company wise prep resource\zs associates\IMG-20240802-WA0068.jpg

questions.pattern: critical reasoning - weaken a substitution claim
questions.title: Health drink vs pulses - weaken the advertiser
questions.statement:
A health drink advertisement says that two spoons of their health drink contain more protein than a bowl of pulses. Therefore, two spoons of the health drink can replace one's need for pulses.

Which of the given statements, if true, would weaken the claim made by the advertiser above?
options: Only a few people exclusively depend on pulses for their protein intake.
The amount of protein requirement varies from person to person.
Pulses provide important nutrients other than protein as well.
The amount of protein provided by a bowl of pulses may not be sufficient for everyone.
questions.answer: Pulses provide important nutrients other than protein as well.
questions.explanation: The claim assumes protein is the only reason people need pulses. If pulses supply other important nutrients, a protein-rich drink cannot fully replace them.

questions.title: Chicken left for 50 people - assumption
questions.statement:
We have chicken left for only about 50 people, so we must buy more.

If the above statement is true, then which of the given statements is an assumption made while making this statement?
options: More than 50 people will partake in chicken.
Chicken is easily available for purchase.
Enough money is available to buy more chicken.
None of the options is an assumption.
questions.answer: More than 50 people will partake in chicken.
questions.explanation: The decision to buy more only makes sense if more than 50 people are expected to eat chicken. That is the assumption the conclusion depends on.

questions.pattern: critical reasoning - weaken a causal conclusion
questions.title: Reverse brain drain 2009 - weaken the argument
questions.statement:
Due to the global economic slowdown in 2008, a new phenomenon was observed in India. Many employees of IT companies working in and professors teaching in the USA were applying for job openings in their motherland, India. Record numbers of this reverse brain drain were seen in 2009. It can, therefore, be concluded that such skilled workers were getting jobs in India.

Which one of the given statements, if true, most seriously weakens the above argument?
options: IT companies and academic institutes in the USA were planning to offer current job positions primarily to people of US origin.
Many IT companies and academic institutes in India were on the lookout for skilled workers with international exposure from developed countries.
Employees of IT companies and academic institutes from the USA applied for job openings in India but a very small percentage of them were able to obtain a suitable position in the country.
Many employees of IT companies and academic institutes from the USA needed to reorient themselves and acquire new skills when they came to work in India.
questions.answer: Employees of IT companies and academic institutes from the USA applied for job openings in India but a very small percentage of them were able to obtain a suitable position in the country.
questions.explanation: The argument moves from 'many applied' to 'they were getting jobs'. If only a small percentage actually got positions, that conclusion fails directly.
source_files: Company wise prep resource-20261001T122326Z-1-001\Company wise prep resource\zs associates\IMG-20240802-WA0071.jpg

questions.title: Commercial writing and fiction creativity - presupposition
questions.statement:
Although working in professions that require commercial writing stimulates creativity, creative thinking related to fiction is underdeveloped in persons working in those professions. The time spent on professional duties does not allow these people to observe society around them. Therefore, people in such professions cannot enhance their creativity to be successful fiction writers.

The above argument presupposes which of the given statements?
options: People who are in creative thinking jobs are not hired for professions requiring commercial writing.
Observing people's behaviour in real-life situations equips people with ideas required for successful fiction writing.
Even during the undertaking of professional duties, people have to think creatively.
Successful fiction writing is mostly imaginary and requires no outside stimulation.
questions.answer: Observing people's behaviour in real-life situations equips people with ideas required for successful fiction writing.
questions.explanation: The argument concludes that lack of time to observe society blocks fiction creativity. That only follows if observing society is what supplies the ideas fiction writing needs.
source_files: Company wise prep resource-20261001T122326Z-1-001\Company wise prep resource\zs associates\IMG-20240802-WA0072.jpg

questions.title: NGO funding with donor conditions - assumption
questions.statement:
A non-governmental organization (NGO) approaches one of its international donors asking for more funding for the coming financial year. The international donor is not completely satisfied with the previous year's outcomes and is placing conditions on the NGO before more funds are sanctioned. The NGO agrees to these conditions and receives the funds immediately.

Which of the given is an assumption (i.e. has no evidence to support it)?
options: The international donor has funds in place so that they can be immediately transferred.
The international donor works with organizations that are not government-controlled.
The NGO would like more funding for the coming financial year and has multiple international donors it could request this from.
In the following year, the NGO will be able to fulfill the conditions placed by its donor.
questions.answer: In the following year, the NGO will be able to fulfill the conditions placed by its donor.
questions.explanation: The passage supports the other three: the funds arrived immediately, the recipient is an NGO, and it has 'one of its international donors'. Nothing in the passage says the NGO will actually meet the conditions.

questions.title: Industrialist on fossil fuels - conclusion
questions.statement:
Industrialist: The increasing demand for energy has made us depend more and more on fossil fuels, which cannot be replenished. This adds to the release of greenhouse gases that adversely affect the environment, resulting in global warming. While it is impractical to seek to reduce energy consumption, we can develop technologies that depend on renewable sources and those that release minimum greenhouse gases.

Which of the given statements can be concluded from the above information?
options: Preserving the remaining non-renewable sources is likely to protect the environment from further damage.
Utilization of renewable resources for energy production is more cost-effective than using conventional sources of energy.
Most of the energy utilization can be shifted to renewable energy sources without a major shift in technologies.
Environmental degradation could be largely contained without significantly decreasing energy consumption.
questions.answer: Environmental degradation could be largely contained without significantly decreasing energy consumption.
questions.explanation: The industrialist argues that cleaner technologies, rather than lower energy use, can address the damage. Cost-effectiveness and 'no major shift in technologies' are never stated.
